flashcards.front_question: List the 8 planets of our Solar System in increasing order of distance from the Sun.
flashcards.back_answer: 1. Mercury, 2. Venus, 3. Earth, 4. Mars, 5. Jupiter, 6. Saturn, 7. Uranus, 8. Neptune.

flashcards.front_question: What is a Constellation? Give two prominent examples.
flashcards.back_answer: A constellation is a group of stars forming a recognizable pattern in the night sky named after figures or objects. Examples: Saptarishi (Ursa Major / Big Dipper) and Orion (The Hunter).

flashcards.front_question: How can you locate the Pole Star (Dhruva Tara) in the northern night sky using Saptarishi?
flashcards.back_answer: Locate the two outer pointer stars on the bowl of the Saptarishi constellation and extend an imaginary straight line upward; the line points directly to the fixed Pole Star marking true North.

flashcards.front_question: Why is Pluto classified as a Dwarf Planet rather than an official planet?
flashcards.back_answer: In 2006, the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto because it has not cleared its orbital neighborhood of other celestial debris.

flashcards.front_question: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is closer to the Sun?
flashcards.back_answer: Venus has a thick atmosphere composed mostly of carbon dioxide, which traps solar heat through an extreme runaway greenhouse effect.
